subject: 40-man roster (MLB)
query: what is the 40-man roster in baseball
title: What is the 40-man roster in baseball? MLB's Nov. 17 deadline, explained
answer: The 40-man roster is the group of up to 40 players a Major League team controls: everyone on the 26-man active roster, players on the 7-, 10- and 15-day injured lists and some minor leaguers. Being on it protects a prospect from the Rule 5 Draft, and the 2026 deadline to add players is Nov. 17.
body:
MLB's glossary says the 40-man roster combines players on the 26-man roster, the 7-, 10- and 15-day injured lists, the bereavement and paternity lists, and some minor leaguers. A team with a full 40-man roster must clear a spot before calling up a minor leaguer who is not on it, for example by moving an injured player to the 60-day injured list. Players on the 40-man roster usually get three option years to be sent to the minors; a player out of options must be designated for assignment and clear waivers first.

Each November, teams decide which prospects to add. Players signed at 18 or younger must be added within five seasons, and those signed at 19 or older within four, or they become eligible to be taken by another team in the Rule 5 Draft. In 2026, the deadline is Nov. 17, followed by the non-tender deadline on Nov. 20.
in_the_news: MLB teams must set their 40-man rosters by Nov. 17, 2026, to protect prospects from the Rule 5 Draft.

faq.q: What is the difference between the 26-man and 40-man roster?
faq.a: The 26-man roster is the active big-league team for games; the 40-man roster includes those 26 plus injured players and some minor leaguers the club controls.

faq.q: When is the 40-man roster deadline for the Rule 5 Draft in 2026?
Does the 60-day injured list count against the 40-man roster?
faq.a: No. Moving a player to the 60-day IL is one way to open a 40-man spot.

faq.q: What does it mean to be added to the 40-man roster?
faq.a: The team protects the player from the Rule 5 Draft and can call him up, but he uses option years when sent to the minors.
